evidence.clarity: 1440: H1 'Lift plans checked against the chart. Signed on site.' plus the lede ('Put in the load, the crane, the radius and the ground... hands it to your appointed person to amend and sign on a tablet') tells a site manager what it does and who signs. The CTA 'Request a pilot on one site' names its object. Nothing later contradicts it.
evidence.fit: Both audiences get a real path. Site manager: 'What it replaces' with a realistic folder of 'LiftPlan_Template_v3 (Block C) FINAL (2).xlsx' files, four handover steps tagged by role, and a pilot block listing what is included and what is asked of the contractor. Appointed person: 'Liftplan doesn't decide whether a lift goes ahead', 'does / does not' lists, and the demo verdicts end with 'The appointed person chooses'. Reading as the AP who distrusts software, though: the demo footer and check row 3 say capacity is 'interpolated between radii', the demo sorts lifts into critical or standard by threshold ('can run under your standard lift plan'), and the worst-outrigger pressure uses a 70% rule that appears only in a code comment, not on the page.
evidence.distinctiveness: Hi-vis yellow hero, an elevation drawing of the crane whose boom, hook and radius dimension move with the slider, the redacted pilot-name bar, the 'Change on the day' stamp on the signed record. Remove the logo and it still reads as a lifting-operations page.
evidence.proof: 1440: an operable lift check sits beside the H1 in the first viewport and opens at 109% with 'Exceeds chart at 14.0 m' in red, so a visitor sees a flag straight away. The LP-0218 signed record lower down is internally consistent (161 kN/m2 on 2.25 m2 mats becomes 91 kN/m2 on 4 m2 steel). The demo shows the checks, not the plan document you would actually get. That document appears only as a static list of sections further down.
evidence.craft: The type and borders are strong and consistent at 1440 and 768. At 390 the SVG labels in the elevation drawing ('chart 13.8 t', 'R 11.0 m', load label) scale to about 7px and are unreadable. The header 'Request a pilot' button is 37px tall, and the inputs and selects are 40px.
evidence.mobile: 390: no overflow and the hero stacks cleanly. There is no menu, because the nav is simply hidden, so the section links are gone. The radius slider is 16px tall. When you drag radius at 390 (slider at y=412), the results sit at y=811-960 and the verdicts at y=972-1202, so only the drawing changes in view and the verdict is off-screen. Targets are 37-40px.
evidence.honesty: 'Sample chart. Not for use on site.' sits in the demo header, and the footer disclaimer is good. 'We are not going to put numbers here that we can't stand behind yet' is excellent. However, the LP-0218 signed record (with times 06:42 and 09:15) has no visible 'example' label; it is marked as an example only in aria-label, so it can read as a real pilot record. The page also invents pilot facts the brief does not give: 'Kept alongside: their existing paper process, for the whole pilot', a Week 1 / Weeks 2-8 / Week 8 schedule, and an offer to put visitors in touch with a site manager. The footer mailto pilots@liftplan.example is not supplied by the brief.
evidence.interaction: Operated at 1440, 768 and 390. Load, rigging, crane, radius (keyboard arrows), ground and mats all recalculate, the drawing moves, and there are no console errors. 'Made ground' gives 'Ground not established'. Switching to the 25 t city crane clamps the radius to 22 m. There is no reset. An empty or negative load ('-5') is silently treated as 0 and reports 'Within 75% of chart, 65%' with no error state. A load of 99999 is accepted ('99999.9 t... 7692296 %').
evidence.copy: Site-specific and written rather than defaulted: 'so nobody has to by torchlight', 'goes back to the appointed person, not onto a Post-it', 'Long enough to cover real critical lifts, short enough to walk away from', 'An appointed person willing to tell us what is wrong with it'. Terms stay consistent throughout.
evidence.first_screen: 1440: the H1, lede, CTA and a working lift check with the crane drawing and 109% utilisation are all in view. A specific promise is backed by an artifact. 390: the H1, lede and full-width CTA are in view, but only the 'Lift check' header and the first two inputs of the artifact show at the bottom. No result is visible.

problems: For the appointed person it advertises interpolating between chart radii and classifies lifts as critical or standard itself, the two things a sceptical AP expects software not to do. The worst-outrigger pressure rule is not stated on the page.
The signed LP-0218 record has no visible 'example' label, and the page invents pilot details (paper kept alongside, an 8-week schedule) plus an email address the brief did not supply.

Phone: no menu, a 16px slider, 37-40px targets, demo feedback below the fold when operating radius, and unreadable ~7px drawing labels. The demo has no reset and silently accepts empty or negative load.

evidence.clarity: H1 'Lift plans that read the load chart for you' plus 'Liftplan is a lift plan app for construction sites. Enter the load, the crane, the radius and the ground; it checks them against the load chart and writes the plan your appointed person signs on a tablet.' A stranger can repeat it. The CTA 'Request a site pilot' sits beside 'A pilot runs on one site. Your appointed person still signs every lift.'
evidence.fit: The appointed-person tension is resolved in substance. The radius hint says 'Rounded up to the next chart row, never interpolated'. The 75% outrigger rule is printed as 'a sample rule for this page'. Section 6 of the sheet leaves 'Lift category' and 'Method and sequence' as 'Decided by the appointed person', with dashed signature boxes, and the 'Filled by Liftplan / Decided by the appointed person' split repeats this. The site-manager path is thin: the pilot is one paragraph ('A pilot starts with one site and its next critical lifts') with nothing on what the contractor must provide or how long it takes, and the replaced spreadsheet gets one sentence.
evidence.distinctiveness: Hazard-tape strip under a sticky header, condensed stencil-like caps, a monospace plan sheet with an 'LP-SAMPLE-01' number, and a chart-row strip that highlights the row in use. It clearly belongs to lifting, though the section structure below the demo is plainer than A's.
evidence.proof: 1440: 'Check a sample lift' starts at y=462 with the 68% readout and the actual lift-plan sheet in the first viewport. The sheet is the deliverable a site manager buys: load, configuration, the chart row used, ground, chart check, and AP boxes. The numbers are consistent: 12.0 + 0.9 = 12.9 t; 12.9/19.0 = 68%; 0.75 x (60 + 12.9) = 54.7 t; 54.7/4.0 = 13.7 t/m2.
evidence.craft: A clean type scale and a consistent 2px rule system. No overflow at 1440, 768 or 390. Minor: at 390 the sticky readout (top 64px) sits over the hazard tape, and the toy border peeks out around it while scrolling. The plan sheet becomes a long column of about 2000px on the phone.
evidence.mobile: 390: the menu button opens a panel with three links and the CTA. Escape closes it. Tapping 'Who signs' closes the menu and lands at the heading. The CTA is full width at 48px, the sliders are 44px tall and the selects 48px. Dragging radius at 390 keeps the black readout stuck at y=64-219, so the result and stamp stay beside your thumb. Weaknesses: the sheet is a long scroll, and the readout covers about a quarter of the screen while you are in the controls.
evidence.honesty: Each label sits where it applies: 'Sample lift and chart, written for this page. Not a manufacturer's chart.' in the demo header (visible at 390), 'a sample rule for this page' under the ground figures, 'Sample thresholds: flagged above 75 %, not issued above 90 %.' in the check, and 'Liftplan never signs.' The pilot copy says 'there are no logos here'. The only addition beyond the brief is 'They have asked not to be named yet', which is a mild embellishment.
evidence.interaction: Operated at 1440, 768 and 390 by keyboard (Arrow, Home, End) and select. States seen: 'Within chart' at 68%; 'Not issued' at 94% above the 90% threshold; 268% exceeding the chart; 'no chart row' at 34 m ('The 30 m boom chart ends at 24 m'); 40 m boom at 4 m ('no chart row under 6 m'); and on soft ground a chart pass with ground failure ('mats of at least 5.0 m2 per outrigger needed'). 'Reset to the sample lift' restores 68%. The sliders cannot take empty or negative values. No console errors.
evidence.copy: Specific and terse: 'Four boxes in. Every number comes off the chart.', 'A pass on the chart with a fail on the ground is still not issued.', 'Go or no-go on the day: Wind, ground after rain, visibility'. Every button says what happens. The page is short and the closing pilot section repeats the hero's 'beside' line word for word.
evidence.first_screen: 1440: the H1, subline, CTA with its pilot explanation, and the sample readout ('68 % of chart / Within chart') plus the top of the plan sheet are all in one viewport. 390: the H1, subline, full-width CTA, the 'Check a sample lift' header with its sample label, and the 68% readout are all visible above y=844.

problems: The site manager's path is thin. There is no account of what a pilot involves (effort, duration, what the contractor supplies), and the spreadsheet being replaced gets a single sentence.
'Not issued above 90 %' presents the software as refusing a lift outright. It is labelled a sample threshold, but an AP may read it as the tool overriding a call that should be theirs.
On the phone the plan sheet is a long column (about 2000px), and the sticky readout overlaps the hazard tape and covers about a quarter of the screen while you are in the controls.

reason: As the appointed person, B earns trust where it matters. It rounds up to the next chart row and never interpolates, prints its sample rules, and leaves lift category, method and signature visibly to the AP on the actual plan sheet the demo produces. Every sample is labelled where it appears, and the phone experience works. A has the stronger voice and the richer site-manager story. I would switch to A if interpolation and threshold-based critical/standard classification were acceptable to the client's appointed persons, and if the unlabelled signed record and the invented pilot details were fixed.
